b2017a81e5e5c532.text: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being considered as tools for computational social science, yet their implications for survey and public-opinion research remain insufficiently understood. This study examines whether and how they can serve as methodological instruments for estimating aggregate public opinion under out-of-sample conditions. Across three studies, commercial and open-source LLMs are evaluated against recent Pew Research Centre surveys. Study 1 shows that GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 can approximate national-level response distributions more accurately than uniform, normal-distribution, and historical-average baselines, with GPT-4 achieving mean absolute errors of approximately 4–8.5%. However, the models also exhibit important threats to validity, including underrepresentation of Republican viewpoints, underestimation of uncertainty, and, in some cases, overly homogeneous response distributions. Study 2 extends the analysis to GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and Llama 3.3, showing that aggregate predictive accuracy generalises across models but that partisan alignment and distributional fidelity are model- and topic-dependent. Study 3 demonstrates that collective-level estimation is more valid than aggregating persona-based individual simulations, which produce substantially higher error and stronger homogeneity bias. Ablation tests further indicate that predictions are relatively robust to role prompts and temperature settings but sensitive to survey-item context. These findings suggest that LLMs may be useful as exploratory and supplementary tools in public-opinion research. However, the responsible use of LLMs requires explicit validation against human data, attention to bias and uncertainty, and careful integration with established principles of survey design.
b2017a81e5e5c532.abstract_zh: 大语言模型越来越多地被当作计算社会科学的工具，但它们在调查和民意研究中的适用性还不清楚。作者做了三项研究，把商用和开源模型与 Pew Research Center 的近期调查对比，检验模型能否在样本外条件下估计总体的民意分布。研究一发现 GPT-3.5 和 GPT-4 估计全国层面回答分布的准确度高于均匀分布、正态分布和历史均值三种基线，GPT-4 的平均绝对误差约 4–8.5%。但模型存在明显的效度威胁：共和党观点被低估，不确定性被低估，部分情况下回答分布过于同质。研究二把分析扩展到 GPT-4o、GPT-4o-mini 和 Llama 3.3，发现总体预测准确度可以跨模型泛化，但党派对齐程度和分布保真度取决于具体模型和话题。研究三比较了两种估计方式，直接在集体层面估计比先给每个虚拟人格做个体模拟再汇总更有效，后者误差明显更高、同质性偏差更强。消融实验显示预测对角色提示词和温度设置相对稳健，但对调查题目的上下文敏感。作者的结论是，大语言模型可以作为民意研究中的探索性和补充性工具，但负责任的使用需要与人类数据做显式验证，关注偏差和不确定性，并谨慎结合既有的调查设计原则。
b2017a81e5e5c532.why: 它给出了大模型模拟民意的误差量级和失效模式（党派偏差、同质性偏差、个体人格模拟不如集体估计），对任何想用 LLM 智能体生成合成调查样本的人都是直接的效度证据和风险清单。

brief.question: LLM 能否在样本外条件下作为方法论工具估计总体公众意见分布
brief.setup: 三项研究，用商业与开源 LLM（GPT-3.5、GPT-4、GPT-4o、GPT-4o-mini、Llama 3.3）模拟回答问卷，与 Pew Research Centre 近期调查对比
brief.method: 比较集体层面估计与基于 persona 的个体模拟聚合两种方式，并做消融测试（role prompts、temperature、survey-item context）
brief.findings: GPT-4 平均绝对误差约 4–8.5%，优于均匀分布、正态分布和历史均值基线；共和党观点被低估，不确定性被低估，部分回答分布过于同质；集体层面估计比 persona 个体模拟聚合更有效，后者误差更高且同质化偏差更强；预测对 role prompts 和 temperature 较稳健，对 survey-item context 敏感；党派对齐与分布保真度随模型和话题变化
brief.validation: 与 Pew Research Centre 真实调查数据对比，误差 4–8.5%，并含消融测试，验证强度较高
brief.limits: 共和党观点代表性不足、不确定性低估、回答分布同质化，且这些偏差随模型和话题变化，作者要求使用前对照人类数据验证
brief.reuse: 作者提出的做法：集体层面估计优于 persona 个体模拟聚合；使用时需对照人类数据验证并遵循既有问卷设计原则

bbc9b4d66e7e40f5.text: Prior work has shown that large language models (LLMs) express implicit biases in high-publicity, one-off decision scenarios such as hiring and intelligence assessment. However, as people increasingly employ autonomous, LLM-powered AI agents that make decisions on their behalf in doing day-to-day tasks, it is of critical importance that we understand how implicit biases, based on sociodemographic assumptions, emerge across a broad milieu of workaday decision scenarios. We used the 17 domains of daily activity in the American Time Use Survey (ATUS) to generate an atlas of 506 decision scenarios in which LLMs --- endowed with personas representing different races, gender identities, and political ideologies --- expressed significant implicit bias. Next, in a crowdsourced audit, 500 participants made 8,010 binary choices about which implicitly biased decision scenarios most deserved further review. We found that participants prioritized decision scenarios that had broad relevance (e.g., about food choices), were high stakes (e.g., about health), and where all members of a simulated sociodemographic group made unanimous decisions (because it was a clear indication of stereotyping). They were less swayed by the magnitude of an observed disparity or the specific ATUS domain the decision scenario represented. When examining the rationale behind their prioritization choices, we found that participants often interpreted disparities as traits of demographic groups and judged whether those traits seemed plausible, often based on their own internalized stereotypes. We discuss implications for building personalized AI agents, digital twins, social simulations, and for using crowdsourced bias audits.
bbc9b4d66e7e40f5.abstract_zh: 已有研究表明，大语言模型在招聘、智力评估这类高曝光度的一次性决策场景中会表达隐性偏见。但随着人们越来越多地让自主运行的LLM智能体代自己处理日常事务，理解隐性偏见如何在更广泛的日常决策场景中浮现就变得很关键。研究团队以American Time Use Survey（ATUS，美国时间使用调查）的17个日常活动领域为基础，构建了一个包含506个决策场景的图谱，让被赋予不同种族、性别认同和政治意识形态人格设定的LLM在这些场景中做决策，并检测其中表现出显著隐性偏见的场景。接着他们开展了一次众包审计，500名参与者共做出8010个二元选择，判断哪些存在隐性偏见的决策场景最值得进一步审查。结果发现，参与者优先选择那些具有广泛相关性的场景（比如关于食物选择的）、高风险的场景（比如关于健康的），以及模拟的某个社会人口群体所有成员做出完全一致决策的场景，因为这种一致性是刻板印象的明显信号。相比之下，观察到的差距幅度大小以及决策场景所属的ATUS领域类别对参与者的优先级判断影响较小。在分析参与者给出优先级判断的理由时，研究者发现参与者常常把差距解读为人口群体的固有特质，并基于自己内化的刻板印象来判断这些特质看起来是否合理。作者讨论了这些发现对构建个性化AI智能体、数字孪生、社会仿真以及开展众包偏见审计的意义。
bbc9b4d66e7e40f5.why: 它把LLM隐性偏见的检测从招聘等少数高曝光场景扩展到覆盖日常生活的506个场景图谱，并揭示了众包审计者自身刻板印象会如何干扰偏见优先级判断，对做社会仿真和数字孪生的人是直接相关的风险提示和方法参考。

brief.question: LLM 驱动的智能体在日常决策场景中会表现出哪些基于社会人口学假设的隐性偏见，以及众包评审者会如何决定哪些偏见场景值得优先审查。
brief.setup: 基于 American Time Use Survey (ATUS) 的 17 个日常活动领域生成 506 个决策场景，让带有不同种族、性别认同和政治意识形态 persona 的 LLM 智能体在这些场景中做决策。随后 500 名众包参与者对场景做出 8,010 次二元选择。材料未说明具体使用的 LLM 型号和时间尺度。
brief.method: 先用 ATUS 领域生成决策场景图谱，检测 LLM 智能体在其中表现出的显著隐性偏见，再通过众包审计让参与者投票选出最值得进一步审查的偏见场景，并分析其排序理由。
brief.findings: 参与者优先选择具有广泛相关性（如食物选择）、高风险（如健康）以及模拟群体成员决策完全一致的场景，后者被视为刻板印象的明确信号。观察到的差异幅度和所属 ATUS 领域对排序影响较小。参与者的理由常把差异解读为人群特征，并依据自身内化的刻板印象判断其合理性。
brief.validation: 通过 500 人共 8,010 次二元选择的众包审计验证，材料未说明与真实行为数据或其他基准的定量对比。
brief.reuse: ATUS 17 领域生成决策场景的方法、506 个隐性偏见场景图谱以及众包偏见审计流程，可用于个性化 AI 智能体、digital twins（数字孪生）和社会仿真的偏见审查。材料未说明是否公开代码或数据。

bd48b9b8ec948700.text: Generative artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming both personal and professional life. In this exploratory study, we investigate the potential role of AI in psychotherapy, focusing on systemic family therapy. We designed a simulation in which psychotherapists interacted with ChatGPT in a role-play scenario involving a distressed couple with a young child. Post-session interviews were held to assess participants’ perceptions of empathy, authenticity, risks, and professional implications. Our findings reveal that while AI can simulate empathy and facilitate useful reflection, it lacks the embodied relational presence crucial to therapy. In this article, we first discuss these results in relation to relevant literature on psychotherapy, technology, and AI. We then introduce a theoretical discussion, drawing on Bowen’s theory of emotional triangles, to speculate about the potential of new, implicit or explicit “technosocial triangles” among humans, therapists, and AIs. While this is a hypothesis rather than an empirical conclusion of our study, we argue that Bowen’s framework helps us imagine how AI might reshape relational systems in families and therapy.
bd48b9b8ec948700.abstract_zh: 这是一项探索性研究，关注生成式 AI 在心理治疗中的潜在角色，聚焦系统式家庭治疗。作者设计了一个模拟场景，让心理治疗师与 ChatGPT 进行角色扮演，情境是一对带着年幼孩子的困境夫妻。会话结束后对参与者进行访谈，评估他们对共情感、真实性、风险和职业影响的看法。结果显示，AI 虽然能模拟共情、促成有价值的反思，但缺少治疗所必需的身体化关系在场。作者先把这些结果与心理治疗、技术和 AI 的相关文献放在一起讨论，随后引入 Bowen 的情感三角理论，推测人类、治疗师和 AI 之间可能形成新的隐性或显性的“技术社会三角”。作者明确说明这只是假说而非本研究的实证结论，但认为 Bowen 的框架有助于想象 AI 如何重塑家庭和治疗中的关系系统。材料未说明样本规模等实验细节。
bd48b9b8ec948700.why: 它用真人治疗师与 LLM 的角色扮演模拟来检验 AI 在高关系敏感场景中的能力边界，结论点出共情可模拟但身体在场不可替代，对做人类行为仿真和 AI 替代真人评估的人是有用的反例与风险提示。

bf27d5d9f81b7f18.story:
Plurai 完成 1300 万美元种子轮融资，同时推出 AI 智能体仿真平台。多家媒体报道了这笔融资，信息基本一致。Yahoo Finance 和 Morningstar 的版本把公司定位为“可信、可自我改进的 AI 智能体”提供仿真基础设施，让智能体在模拟环境中训练并自我改进，目标是提升可靠性。另一条报道补充了类比：训练方式类似自动驾驶汽车，用仿真环境来训练智能体。中文来源确认这是种子轮，平台与融资同日发布。各家都没有给出技术路线、客户和仿真场景的细节。

对智能体仿真领域，我推测这笔钱说明投资人认可“先在模拟环境里训练和验证智能体、再上线”这条路线，自动驾驶的类比也暗示领域内正在借用成熟行业的仿真验证方法来补智能体可靠性这块短板。

b32a8ca7c7009a9c.text: Integration Over Numbers: What 5,000 German Wargame Runs Say About Autonomous Fleets Defense.info
b32a8ca7c7009a9c.abstract_zh: 材料只有一条新闻标题，没有正文。标题显示 Defense.info 发表了一篇关于德国兵棋推演的文章，推演共运行了 5000 次，主题是自主舰队（无人水面或水下舰艇编队）。标题给出的核心结论是“整合重于数量”，即自主舰队作战效能更多取决于系统之间的整合程度，而不是舰艇数量本身。材料中没有提供推演的具体设置、参与机构、所用系统、数据结果或验证方式，无法进一步展开。
b32a8ca7c7009a9c.why: 标题指向一个对海战推演有参考价值的结论，即自主系统的整合度可能比数量更影响作战效果，但材料只有标题，需要找到原文才能判断推演方法和结论的可靠性。

b5be1eee63d8b091.text: Large language models understand passengers' driving commands, but as driving agents they reason in generated text for seconds and must infer each action's consequences implicitly from the scene. We present Jev-AD, which pairs Jev, a typed decision model that answers predefined questions with probabilities, not generated text, with a language world model that predicts for every candidate action how nearby vehicles move over the next two seconds. Code turns these predictions into foreseen consequences, which Jev compares instead of inferring them from coordinates. In simulated highway merging (500 car-episodes), this foresight lowers the same decision model's collision rate from 26.0% to 2.4% at 0.25 seconds per decision, and Jev-AD achieves the passenger's intent in 93% of free-form command trials. In 500 replayed real-world NGSIM episodes, foresight lowers the collision rate from 48.2% to 2.8%, and the world model, learned from this traffic, foresees 93% of dangerous actions. Project page: https://ys-qu.github.io/jev-ad-website.
b5be1eee63d8b091.abstract_zh:
大语言模型能听懂乘客的驾驶指令，但作为驾驶智能体，它要在生成的文本里推理数秒，还得从场景坐标里隐式推断每个动作的后果。作者提出 Jev-AD，由两部分组成：Jev 是一个类型化决策模型，用概率回答预设问题，不做文本生成；语言世界模型则对每个候选动作预测附近车辆未来两秒的运动。代码把这些预测转成可预见的后果，Jev 直接比较这些后果，不用再从坐标里推断。

结果方面，在模拟的高速公路汇入场景（500 个车次回合）中，加入这种预见能力后，同一个决策模型的碰撞率从 26.0% 降到 2.4%，每次决策耗时 0.25 秒；在 500 段回放的真实 NGSIM 交通数据中，碰撞率从 48.2% 降到 2.8%。用这些真实交通学出来的世界模型能预判 93% 的危险动作。在自由格式指令试验中，Jev-AD 达成乘客意图的比例为 93%。
b5be1eee63d8b091.why: 它给“LLM 做决策慢且不擅长隐式推演后果”这个问题提供了一个可复用的结构：决策模型只出概率，世界模型负责显式预测，两者分工后在真实交通回放上把碰撞率压到 2.8%，这个思路对任何需要 LLM 智能体在仿真环境里做安全决策的场景都有参考价值。

brief.question: 解决 LLM 作为驾驶智能体时用生成文本推理、耗时数秒且需隐式推断动作后果的问题，实现语言引导的安全自动驾驶。
brief.setup: Jev-AD 由 Jev（一个用概率而非生成文本回答预定义问题的类型化决策模型）和一个语言世界模型组成；仿真环境包括 500 个高速公路汇入 car-episodes 和 500 个回放的真实 NGSIM 场景片段，世界模型预测候选动作后两秒内附近车辆的移动。
brief.method: 语言世界模型对每个候选动作预测周边车辆未来两秒的运动，代码把预测转成可预见的后果，Jev 直接比较这些后果而不是从坐标里隐式推断。
brief.findings: 在模拟高速汇入中，加入 foresight 使同一决策模型的碰撞率从 26.0% 降到 2.4%，每次决策耗时 0.25 秒；在 93% 的自由形式乘客指令试验中实现了乘客意图。在 500 个回放的 NGSIM 片段中，碰撞率从 48.2% 降到 2.8%；从该交通数据学到的世界模型能预见 93% 的危险动作。
brief.validation: 与回放的真实 NGSIM 交通数据对比，碰撞率从 48.2% 降到 2.8%；世界模型对危险动作的预见率在真实数据上为 93%。未说明与人类驾驶员或其他基线方法的直接对比。
brief.reuse: 项目页面 https://ys-qu.github.io/jev-ad-website，未说明是否开源代码与数据。

b3871885fa350a70.text: Multi-vehicle cooperative autonomous driving enhances the safety and reliability of autonomous driving systems through information sharing among connected vehicles, demonstrating significant potential for improving traffic safety. LLM-based approaches leverage strong reasoning capabilities of LLMs to enable effective inter-vehicle negotiation and improve cooperative driving performance. However, driving decisions in complex traffic scenarios are inherently multi-solution in nature. As a result, existing negotiation-based methods often converge prematurely to suboptimal solutions, hindering consensus formation and limiting the practical deployment of cooperative autonomous driving systems. To address this challenge, we propose CoLMIN, the LLM-based multi-decision path negotiation framework for cooperative autonomous driving, achieving stable decision consensus through multi-decision path negotiation and reflective reasoning. To achieve stable and high-quality consensus in cooperative autonomous driving, CoLMIN consists of three key components: (i) an LLM-based Multi-Intent Negotiation module (LMin), which adopts a Negotiator-Evaluator paradigm and generates multiple candidate driving intentions for joint evaluation; (ii) an Evaluation-based Shallow Reflection Module (ESRM), which analyzes negotiation outcomes and provides feedback to guide subsequent negotiations, thereby accelerating consensus formation; and (iii) an LLM-based Deep Reflection Module (LDRM), which performs long-term reflection over negotiation histories to mitigate cognitive fixation and prevent the system from converging to suboptimal solutions. Experimental results in the CARLA simulation environment demonstrate that CoLMIN significantly outperforms existing methods in challenging interactive driving scenarios.

bd8649cc4e583263.text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in interactive systems where understanding user intent precisely is paramount. A key capability for such systems is effective question clarification, especially when user queries are ambiguous or underspecified. This paper introduces a novel tri-agent framework for the robust evaluation of an LLM's ability to engage in clarifying dialogue. Our framework comprises three distinct LLM-based agents: (1) a Question Clarifying Agent (QCA), the system under evaluation, tasked with identifying ambiguities and posing clarifying questions; (2) a Respondent Agent (RA), designed to simulate human user responses, potentially including irrelevant or challenging replies; and (3) an Evaluator Agent (EA), an LLM-as-a-judge, which assesses the quality of the dialogue based on a comprehensive set of metrics. We detail a methodology for synthetic data generation in the supply chain domain as an example. We propose metrics evaluating ambiguity handling, question quality, dialogue efficiency, language appropriateness, and final intent alignment. We also briefly discuss the validation of the EA against human judgments. This work provides a structured approach to benchmark, validate, and improve the clarification capabilities of conversational LLM applications.

b98fd10f807d82f2.text: LLM-based user simulators are increasingly used to evaluate autonomous agents at scale, in place of costly human evaluations. Despite this promise, these simulators exhibit "assistant bias," a tendency to cooperate and pursue task goals. They rarely reproduce the frustration or disengagement that real users exhibit, compromising evaluation validity. Prior work outlines that this bias is baked in during model training, which role-playing prompts fail to override. We analyze this bias from model activations, extracting a user role vector by contrasting how the model represents user versus assistant perspectives on the same dialogue. We observe two findings: (i) the user direction is identifiable in activations, elicits user-like behaviors, and captures characteristics distinct from assistant traits; and (ii) although user-role activation associates with simulation realism and steering strengthens it, it can exaggerate user behaviors and override individual user profiles. Together, our findings provide a representation-level analysis of LLM user simulators, confirming that assistant bias is structurally identifiable and that user behavior can be directionally analyzed.

b027be94af8fb24d.text: Role-playing agents (RPAs) have become one of the most important consumer applications of large language models. Users engage in multi-turn conversations with RPAs for experiences such as emotional comfort, making reliable evaluation essential for measuring capability, comparing systems, and guiding further improvement. Existing benchmarks, however, typically require an RPA to continue a fixed dialogue history and then evaluate the continuation using a fixed rubric detached from the user. We identify and empirically demonstrate two limitations of this design. First, an RPA's output is shaped by the preceding dialogue history, preventing a scientifically grounded assessment of its role-playing ability in real multi-turn settings. Second, user experience varies substantially across individuals, and conventional fixed rubrics need not align with user satisfaction. We therefore introduce PALATE (Person-Aligned LLM-Simulated-User Assessment with Tailored Evaluation), a scalable RPA benchmark built on user simulators. PALATE is accompanied by a pool of 300 character profiles. Its main evaluation trains five per-user simulators and lets them engage candidate RPAs in free-form, multi-turn conversations over a pre-frozen panel of character profiles. Alongside a general quality rubric, we construct personalized rubrics to measure user satisfaction; on held-out annotated data, the personalized rubrics show higher agreement with human judgments than the general rubric. In the main evaluation of 16 candidates, PALATE separately characterizes generic turn quality, long-horizon session capability, and per-user experience on multi-turn trajectories co-constructed by each candidate. It thereby produces interpretable evaluations of specific user-RPA pairs rather than compressing systems into a single user-independent ranking.

bae246750698a18e.text: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents that make consumption decisions on behalf of users. This shift raises fundamental questions for consumer theory, which has traditionally modeled humans as the primary decision-makers. In this paper, we introduce LLM Consumer Behavior Theory, a new field of study concerned with analyzing consumer behavior in agentic markets. Drawing on classical and behavioral economics alongside recent advances in Natural Language Processing, we formalize how human preferences are reflected and acted upon by LLM-based agents, and how agent-level decisions aggregate into market demand. We unify previously fragmented literature on LLM decision-making, human behavior simulation, and preference elicitation under a common economic lens, highlighting where assumptions, such as rationality and heterogeneity, may fail in agentic markets. Rather than providing empirical validation, this paper outlines the scope of LLM consumer behavior and identifies open research questions related to alignment, preference representation, and market dynamics.

b1fd6335c69a72e0.text: LLM-as-user-simulation has become core infrastructure for conversational AI: agent benchmarks (tau-bench), training pipelines, and a growing body of fidelity studies all rely on LLMs role-playing the human side of dialogue. Existing frameworks measure communicative fidelity -- whether simulators talk like humans -- against ground truth from paid participants role-playing assigned goals. We argue this has a structural blind spot: when the goal is assigned, the user's willingness is exogenous, so no framework can test whether simulators make decisions like real users whose motivation is endogenous, latent, and decaying. We introduce decision fidelity -- whether a simulated population reproduces the decision-state dynamics of real users facing real, consequential choices -- and measure it on a unique testbed: 2,790 production conversations between an LLM sales agent and real customers, including 793 with verified payment outcomes. Using a teacher-forced probe protocol that holds context and instrument fixed, we find a systematic, outcome-correlated failure we call the disengagement deficit: simulators reproduce eventual buyers almost exactly (depth bias +0.09) but inflate eventual non-buyers toward the purchase frame (depth bias +0.40; d=0.38, p<0.001), halving expressed resistance (25.1% to 13.5%) and nearly doubling deliberation (21.9% to 40.1%) while fabricating no purchases. The deficit replicates across model families (DeepSeek: d=0.41, p=0.002) and resists the obvious fix: instructing the simulator that it may disengage cuts marginal bias five-fold but barely moves the outcome-conditioned contrast (d=0.34, p=0.008). Real non-buyers say "not now" and stop; simulated non-buyers ask about price. Evaluating or training sales and persuasion agents against such simulators overstates funnel progress exactly where it matters most -- the customers who walk away.
b1fd6335c69a72e0.abstract_zh: LLM 扮演用户已成为对话 AI 的基础设施，tau-bench 等基准、训练管线和保真度研究都依赖它。作者指出已有框架只测“沟通保真度”，即模拟器说话像不像真人，且真值来自被指派目标的付费受试者。目标被指派意味着用户意愿是外生的，这类框架无法检验模拟器在动机内生、潜在且随时间衰减的真实决策上是否像真人。作者提出 decision fidelity，检验模拟人群能否复现真实用户面对有真实后果的选择时的决策状态动态。测试床是 2,790 段 LLM 销售智能体与真实客户的生产对话，其中 793 段有验证过的支付结果。用固定上下文和工具的 teacher-forced 探测协议，作者发现一种与结果相关的系统性失败，称之为 disengagement deficit：模拟器复现最终买家几乎精确（depth bias +0.09），但把最终不买的人往购买语境推（depth bias +0.40；d=0.38，p<0.001），抵抗性表达从 25.1% 降到 13.5%，犹豫表达从 21.9% 升到 40.1%，同时没有伪造购买。该缺陷跨模型家族复现（DeepSeek：d=0.41，p=0.002），且抗简单修复：告诉模拟器可以退出，能把边际偏差降五倍，但结果条件下的对比几乎不变（d=0.34，p=0.008）。真实不买的人说“现在不买”然后停止；模拟的不买者会问价格。作者认为，用这类模拟器评测或训练销售与说服智能体，会在最关键的地方高估漏斗进展，即那些真正走掉的客户。
b1fd6335c69a72e0.why: 它指出了 LLM 用户模拟的一个结构性盲区：现有保真度评测只看沟通层面，而决策层面的失真会让销售类智能体的评测和训练在最关键的流失客户上系统性偏乐观，且简单提示词修复无效。

brief.question: LLM 用户模拟器在对话式 AI（如 tau-bench 基准、训练管线）中被广泛用来扮演人类用户，但现有框架只测交流保真度（说话像不像人），无法测决策保真度：模拟用户面对真实、有后果的选择时，会不会做出像真实用户那样的决策。
brief.setup: 测试床为 2,790 段生产环境对话，来自一个 LLM 销售智能体与真实客户的交流，其中 793 段有已验证的支付结果。模拟器由多个模型家族扮演用户，包括 DeepSeek。
brief.method: 作者提出 decision fidelity 概念，并用 teacher-forced probe protocol 测量：固定上下文和工具不变，让模拟器在真实对话的各个决策点上续写，比较模拟人群与真实用户的决策状态动态。
brief.findings: 发现一种系统性、与结果相关的失败，作者称为 disengagement deficit：模拟器几乎完美复现最终购买者（depth bias +0.09），但把最终不买者往购买方向推（depth bias +0.40；d=0.38，p<0.001），表达抗拒的比例从 25.1% 降到 13.5%，犹豫斟酌从 21.9% 升到 40.1%，但没有凭空捏造购买。该缺陷跨模型家族复现（DeepSeek：d=0.41，p=0.002）。给模拟器加“可以退出”的指令能把边际偏差降五倍，但对结果条件化对比几乎无效（d=0.34，p=0.008）。真实不买者说“现在不买”然后停止，模拟不买者却会问价格。
brief.validation: 与真实生产对话的已验证支付结果对比（793 段），用效应量和显著性检验量化偏差，并跨模型家族复现、做了指令干预的消融实验。强度较高：基于真实成交结果而非付费参与者角色扮演。
brief.limits: 作者指出用这类模拟器评估或训练销售、说服类智能体会高估漏斗进展，尤其在高流失客户处；材料未说明测试床是否限于单一销售场景或单一 LLM 销售智能体。
brief.reuse: teacher-forced probe protocol（固定上下文与工具、在决策点探测模拟器行为）和 decision fidelity、depth bias 这套测量框架可直接用于评估用户模拟器；数据集是否公开未说明。

b5c0748305213a37.text: Equipping Large Language Models (LLMs) with human-like personas is crucial for agentic applications, such as role-play and user simulation. Traditional prompt-based methods rely on descriptive conditioning by injecting static textual profiles, which often makes agents show generic behaviors due to a lack of realistic life memory. To fill this gap, we introduce memory-based conditioning, a paradigm inspired by the cognitive psychology, which replaces abstract profiles with an autobiographical memory base, enabling frozen LLMs to dynamically retrieve situation-relevant memory to guide their behaviors. We formalize its enabling task as customized lifelong memory synthesis and propose MemoryForge, a novel framework to synthesize such lifelong memory from brief target personas. MemoryForge has three key components: a context generator for socio-historical grounding, a life organizer for developmental coherence toward the target identity, and a multi-resolution simulator that balances broad temporal summaries with high-fidelity episodic experiences. Experiments on PersonaGym for role-play and SimulatorArena for user-simulation, show that the synthesized memory base by MemoryForge enables frozen LLMs to exhibit more human-like behaviors than strong descriptive conditioning baselines across multiple metrics and LLM backbones.

b6469672b92c7679.text: LLMs are increasingly deployed to simulate social interactions, yet many of the existing simulators remain ad hoc and monolithic. This lack of architectural standardization prevents reproducible research and complicates downstream evaluation. We advance a rigorous science of LLM-based multi-agent simulation by modularizing core components into Environments, Agents, Simulation engines, and Evaluation metrics (EASE). We demonstrate the utility of EASE configuration by wrapping it in an experimental study schema for orchestrating workflows centered around answering explicit research questions in generated scenarios. We contribute SiliSocS, an open-source, research-ready Silicon Society Sandbox implementing a study-structured EASE configuration to enable highly configurable and reproducible LLM-based social simulations. Using SiliSocS and EASE, we present three case studies, showcasing the system's comprehensive assessment of existing questions, ability to dive deeper into complex questions, and elaboration of existing studies, respectively. Together, these case studies highlight the limitations of current modeling approaches and isolate the impacts of design choices on key results.
b6469672b92c7679.abstract_zh:
LLM 越来越多地被用来模拟社会互动，但现有的仿真器大多是临时搭建的单体系统，没有统一的架构标准。作者认为这阻碍了可复现研究，也让下游评测变得困难。

做法上，作者把 LLM 多智能体仿真的核心组件模块化为四类：环境（Environments）、智能体（Agents）、仿真引擎（Simulation engines）和评测指标（Evaluation metrics），合称 EASE 配置。他们把 EASE 包装进一个实验研究模式，用来编排以明确研究问题为中心的工作流，在生成的场景中回答这些问题。在此之上，作者发布了 SiliSocS，一个开源、面向研究的“硅基社会”沙盒，实现了按研究结构组织的 EASE 配置，支持高度可配置、可复现的 LLM 社会仿真。

作者用 SiliSocS 和 EASE 做了三个案例研究，分别展示系统对已有问题的全面评估能力、对复杂问题的深入挖掘能力，以及对已有研究的扩展能力。这些案例揭示了当前建模范式的局限，并分离出设计选择对关键结果的影响。
b6469672b92c7679.why: 它给了 LLM 社会仿真一个可复用的模块化架构和开源沙盒，做仿真推演的研究者可以直接拿它来组织实验、分离设计选择的影响，也适合作为对照基准检查自己系统的可复现性。

brief.validation: 未说明（材料未提及与真实数据或人类行为的对比）。
brief.limits: 材料提到当前建模方法存在局限，且现有仿真器 ad hoc、单体式影响可复现性，但未给出具体局限细节。
brief.reuse: SiliSocS 是开源、research-ready 的硅社会沙盘，实现了 study-structured 的 EASE 配置，读者可直接用于搭建可配置、可复现的 LLM 社会仿真。

b9226356760a196a.text: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) with microscopic traffic simulation offers a promising path toward autonomous urban planning and intelligent transportation analysis. However, existing monolithic agent architectures often struggle with the complexity of end-to-end simulation workflows, leading to reasoning failures, parameter inconsistency, and a lack of systematic state management. This paper proposes a novel multi-agent collaborative framework designed to automate the entire lifecycle of traffic simulation in SUMO (Simulation of Urban Mobility). Our approach decouples the simulation pipeline into specialized roles, including Planner, Builder, Demand, Runner, and Analyst, coordinated by a high-level reasoning engine. We introduce a state-persistent Orchestrator leveraging the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to ensure seamless data handover and environmental consistency across distributed agent actions. This architecture enables a robust closed-loop refinement process, where simulation outcomes are iteratively analyzed and optimized to satisfy user-defined Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Experimental results through role ablation studies demonstrate that the proposed multi-agent framework significantly enhances task success rates and parameter accuracy compared to single-agent baselines. Furthermore, case studies on real-world network extraction and traffic optimization highlight the system's capability to bridge the gap between high-level natural language intent and low-level simulation execution.
b9226356760a196a.abstract_zh: 把大语言模型接入 SUMO 微观交通仿真，有望支撑自动化的城市规划与交通分析，但现有单体智能体架构难以应对端到端仿真流程的复杂性，容易出现推理失败、参数不一致和状态管理缺失的问题。作者提出一个多智能体协作框架，把仿真流水线拆解成专职角色：Planner、Builder、Demand、Runner 和 Analyst，由一个高层推理引擎协调。框架引入保持状态的 Orchestrator，基于 Model Context Protocol（MCP）保证分布式智能体动作之间的数据交接和环境一致性。这套架构支持闭环改进：仿真结果被迭代分析和优化，直到满足用户定义的 KPI。角色消融实验表明，与单智能体基线相比，该框架显著提高了任务成功率和参数准确率。作者还做了真实路网提取和交通优化的案例研究，展示系统能把高层自然语言意图落地为底层仿真执行。局限方面，材料未提及与真实交通数据的定量校准，验证主要来自消融实验和案例研究。
b9226356760a196a.why: 它给出了一个可复用的多智能体分工加 MCP 状态管理方案，解决 LLM 驱动仿真器时参数不一致和流程失控的痛点，对想做自然语言到仿真流水线自动化的研究者有直接参考价值。

b161517befe3515a.text: The integration of large language models (LLMs) in economic simulations has significantly enhanced agent-based modeling, yet existing frameworks struggle to capture the interplay between short-term optimization and long-term strategic planning. Conventional approaches rely on static data-driven predictions, failing to incorporate adaptive behaviors influenced by economic sentiment, market volatility, and individual goals. To address these limitations, we introduce a novel EconAI framework, incorporating economic sentiment indexing (ESI), memory weighting, and dynamic decision-making mechanisms. By quantifying economic belief, adjusting historical data influence, and linking work-consumption behaviors, EconAI achieves a more human-like decision process, where agents adapt their actions based on both market signals and long-term objectives. It is the first LLM-powered simulation system that can simulate the macro/microeconomic environment and interactions in a unified framework. Empirical evaluations show that EconAI improves stability in economic responses, better replicates real-world employment-consumption cycles, and enhances overall decision robustness. This advancement marks a crucial step towards more realistic, adaptive economic agent simulations.
b161517befe3515a.abstract_zh: 现有 LLM 经济仿真难以刻画短期优化与长期战略规划之间的相互作用，传统方法依赖静态的数据驱动预测，没有纳入经济情绪、市场波动和个体目标带来的适应性行为。作者为此提出 EconAI 框架，包含三个机制：经济情绪指数（ESI）用来量化经济信念，记忆权重机制调整历史数据对决策的影响，再加上动态决策机制把工作与消费行为关联起来。这样智能体的决策过程更接近人类，会同时根据市场信号和长期目标调整行动。作者称 EconAI 是第一个能在统一框架内同时模拟宏观和微观经济环境及其交互的 LLM 仿真系统。实验评估显示，EconAI 提高了经济响应的稳定性，更好地复现了真实世界的就业-消费周期，整体决策稳健性也得到增强。摘要没有给出具体实验设置和量化指标，验证细节需要看正文。
b161517befe3515a.why: 它给出了可复用的设计：用情绪指数和记忆权重让 LLM 智能体在动态经济环境里做带长期目标的决策，对做经济和市场仿真的研究者是直接的方法参考。

b09bbd94bc8c2f68.text: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate human populations via persona prompting, often under the assumptions that richer persona descriptions improve behavioral fidelity, similarly sized attribute combinations are equally simulatable, and persona definitions generalize across tasks. In this work, we formalize these assumptions and systematically evaluate them across multiple architectures, scales, and simulation settings. We identify a fundamental limitation we term persona manifold collapse, where increasingly expressive persona specifications lead to systematic contraction of representational and behavioral diversity. Across models, increasing persona complexity consistently reduces inter-persona separation in latent space and weakens behavioral differentiation in downstream simulation tasks. These effects persist across multiple analyses as richer personas fail to preserve human subgroup disagreement, performance varies across attribute combinations of similar size, and adding descriptive detail often degrades rather than improves simulation fidelity. Surprisingly, simple Age-Gender personas consistently outperform richly specified Ideal Customer Profiles (ICPs) across industries, achieving substantially higher downstream prediction accuracy. We find that collapse is not uniform across attributes. Certain combinations remain behaviorally stable and preserve stronger alignment with human responses, forming localized regions we term alignment bridges. Together, our results provide empirical and conceptual foundations for understanding the limits of persona-conditioned simulation, highlighting the need for representation-aware persona construction rather than increasing persona expressivity alone.
b09bbd94bc8c2f68.abstract_zh: LLM 常通过人设提示来模拟人类群体，背后有三个常见假设：人设描述越丰富，行为保真度越高；规模相近的属性组合可模拟性相当；人设定义能跨任务泛化。作者把这三个假设形式化，在多种模型架构、规模和仿真设置下做了系统评测。核心发现是一个被作者称为 persona manifold collapse 的现象：人设规格越有表达力，表征多样性和行为多样性的收缩越系统化。跨模型的结果一致，增加人设复杂度会缩小潜空间中人设之间的距离，削弱下游仿真任务中的行为分化。更丰富的描述常常降低而非提升模拟保真度，也无法保留人类子群体之间的分歧，且规模相近的属性组合之间表现差异明显。最反直觉的结果是，简单的年龄-性别人设在多个行业里都稳定优于精心构造的理想客户画像（ICP），下游预测准确率明显更高。坍缩并非在所有属性上均匀发生，某些属性组合在行为上保持稳定、与人类回答对齐更强，作者把这些局部区域称为 alignment bridges。结论是，人设条件模拟需要表征感知的人设构造，单纯提高人设表达力行不通。
b09bbd94bc8c2f68.why: 它用实证推翻了'人设越详细模拟越准'的默认做法，给做人类行为仿真的研究者提供了可操作的人设构造原则和坍缩这一新概念。

brief.question: 检验 persona prompting 模拟人类群体的三个常见假设：更丰富的 persona 描述是否提升行为保真度、规模相近的属性组合是否同样可模拟、persona 定义是否跨任务泛化。
brief.setup: 在多个模型架构、规模和仿真设置下评估 persona 条件化模拟，材料未说明具体智能体数量、环境与时间尺度。
brief.method: 形式化上述假设并系统评估，测量 latent space 中 persona 间分离度与下游仿真任务中的行为分化，比较不同复杂度与属性组合的 persona。
brief.findings: 发现 persona manifold collapse：persona 表达越丰富，latent space 中 persona 间分离度系统性收缩，下游行为分化减弱；简单 Age-Gender persona 在多个行业中持续优于详细定义的 Ideal Customer Profiles (ICPs)，下游预测准确率明显更高；部分属性组合保持行为稳定并保留与人类回答的更强对齐，称为 alignment bridges。
brief.validation: 与人类子群体分歧程度对比，检验 persona 是否保留人类 subgroup disagreement；跨多个架构、规模和仿真设置重复分析。材料未给出具体误差数字。
brief.limits: collapse 在不同属性间不均匀；增加描述细节常降低而非提升仿真保真度，说明仅提高 persona 表达力不足，需要 representation-aware 的 persona 构造。

b56883435d2a519d.text: User simulators are increasingly leveraged to build interactive AI assistants, yet how to measure the quality of these simulators remains an open question. In this work, we show how simulator quality can be quantified in terms of its downstream utility: how an LLM assistant trained with this user simulator performs in the wild when interacting with real humans. In a controlled experiment where only the user simulator varies, we train LLM assistants via reinforcement learning against a spectrum of simulators, from an LLM prompted to role-play a user to one fine-tuned on human utterances from WildChat. As evaluation, we measure pairwise win rates in a user study with 283 participants and on WildBench, a benchmark derived from real human--AI conversations. Training against the role-playing LLM yields an assistant statistically indistinguishable from the initial assistant in our user study (51% win rate), whereas training against the fine-tuned simulator yields significant gains (58% over the initial and 57% over the one trained against role-playing). Closer inspection reveals three further patterns: methods for making role-playing LLMs more realistic (e.g., persona conditioning) improve trained assistants but do not close the gap to the fine-tuned simulator; scaling the simulator's model size benefits the fine-tuned simulator but yields no gain for role-playing ones; and assistants trained against role-playing simulators fail to generalize when paired with other simulators at test time, while the one trained against fine-tuned simulator does. Together, these results argue for grounding user simulators in real human behavior and measuring their quality by their downstream effect on real users.
b56883435d2a519d.abstract_zh: 用户模拟器被越来越多地用来构建交互式 AI 助手，但如何衡量模拟器的质量一直没有定论。作者提出一个衡量标准：模拟器的质量体现在下游效用上，即用它训练出的 LLM 助手在真实人类交互中的表现。实验设计上，作者只改变用户模拟器这一个变量，用强化学习训练一系列 LLM 助手，模拟器从一个被提示扮演用户的 LLM，到一个在 WildChat 人类真实对话上微调的 LLM。评测分两部分：283 人参与的用户研究中的成对胜率，以及基于真实人机对话的基准 WildBench。结果显示，用角色扮演 LLM 训练的助手在用户研究中与初始助手无统计差异（胜率 51%），而用微调模拟器训练的助手显著更好，对初始助手胜率 58%，对角色扮演版本胜率 57%。作者进一步发现三个规律：让角色扮演 LLM 更真实的方法（如人格条件化）能改进训练出的助手，但追不上微调模拟器；扩大模拟器的模型规模对微调模拟器有帮助，对角色扮演模拟器没有收益；用角色扮演模拟器训练的助手在测试时换成其他模拟器就无法泛化，用微调模拟器训练的助手则可以。这些结果支持把用户模拟器建立在真实人类行为上，并用对真实用户的下游影响来衡量其质量。
b56883435d2a519d.why: 它给出了一个可操作的模拟器质量标准（下游真人效用），并用对照实验证明角色扮演式 LLM 模拟器训练效果接近于零，这对所有用 LLM 模拟人类做训练或推演的人都是直接警示。

b2c485b53a59b6fb.text: Social simulation is essential for understanding collective human behavior by modeling how individual interactions give rise to large-scale social dynamics. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled multi-agent frameworks with human-like reasoning and communication capabilities. However, existing LLM-based simulations treat social networks as fixed communication scaffolds, failing to leverage the structural signals that shape behavioral convergence and heterogeneous influence in real-world systems, which often leads to inefficient and unrealistic dynamics. To address this challenge, we propose TopoSim, a unified topology-aware social simulation framework that explicitly integrates structural reasoning into agent interactions along two complementary dimensions. First, TopoSim aligns agents with similar structural roles and interaction contexts into shared backbone units, enabling coordinated updates that reduce redundant computation while preserving emergent social dynamics. Second, TopoSim models social influence as a structure-induced signal, introducing heterogeneous interaction patterns grounded in network topology rather than uniform influence assumptions. Extensive experiments across three social simulation frameworks and diverse datasets demonstrate that TopoSim achieves comparable or improved simulation fidelity while reducing token consumption by 50 - 90%. Moreover, our approach more accurately reproduces key structural phenomena observed in real-world social systems and exhibits strong generalization and scalability.

b032625e88685139.text: Governing common-pool resources requires agents to develop enduring strategies through cooperation and self-governance to avoid collective failure. While foundation models have shown potential for cooperation in these settings, existing multi-agent research provides little insight into whether structured leadership and election mechanisms can improve collective decision making. The lack of such a critical organizational feature ubiquitous in human society presents a significant shortcoming of the current methods. In this work we aim to directly address whether leadership and elections can support improved social welfare and cooperation through multi-agent simulation with LLMs. We present our open-source framework that simulates leadership through elected personas and candidate-driven agendas and carry out an empirical study of LLMs under controlled governance conditions. Our experiments demonstrate that having elected leadership improves social welfare scores by 55.4% and survival time by 128.6% across a range of high performing LLMs. Through the construction of an agent social graph we compute centrality metrics to assess the social influence of leader personas and also analyze rhetorical and cooperative tendencies revealed through a sentiment analysis on leader utterances. This work lays the foundation for further study of election mechanisms in multi-agent systems toward navigating complex social dilemmas.
b032625e88685139.abstract_zh: 治理公共池塘资源要求智能体通过合作与自我治理形成持久策略，避免集体失败。已有基础模型研究显示了一定的合作潜力，但现有多智能体研究几乎没有考察结构化领导与选举机制能否改进集体决策，而这类组织特征在人类社会中无处不在。作者直接研究领导与选举能否通过 LLM 多智能体仿真提升社会福祉与合作。他们构建了一个开源框架，用被选举出来的人格（elected personas）和候选人驱动的议程来模拟领导，并在受控治理条件下对多款 LLM 做实证研究。实验表明，引入选举领导让社会福祉得分提高 55.4%，存活时间延长 128.6%，结果在多款高性能 LLM 上一致。作者还构建了智能体社会图，计算中心性指标来衡量领导者人格的社会影响力，并对领导者的发言做情感分析，考察其修辞与合作倾向。这项工作为多智能体系统中选举机制的进一步研究打下基础，用于应对复杂的社会困境。材料未报告与真实人类群体数据的对比验证。
b032625e88685139.why: 它把选举和领导机制引入 LLM 多智能体合作研究，给出了可复用的开源框架和跨多款 LLM 的一致量化结果，适合做治理机制与集体决策仿真的研究者直接跟进。

brief.question: 研究选举产生的领导层能否改善 LLM 多智能体系统在公共池塘资源治理中的合作与社会福利，避免集体失败。
brief.setup: 开源多智能体仿真框架，智能体由多个高性能 LLM 驱动，通过选举产生 leader persona 并由候选人提出议程（agenda），在受控治理条件下进行公共资源治理实验。具体智能体数量、环境细节和时间尺度未说明。
brief.method: 模拟选举机制产生领导角色，候选人提出议程驱动治理；构建 agent social graph 计算中心性指标衡量 leader 的社会影响力；对 leader 话语做情感分析，考察修辞与合作倾向。
brief.findings: 有选举领导层的条件下，社会福利得分提高 55.4%，生存时间提高 128.6%，结果在多个高性能 LLM 上成立。
brief.validation: 未说明（材料未提及与真实数据或人类基线的对比、消融实验细节）。
brief.limits: 未说明（材料仅提到现有研究缺乏对领导与选举机制的洞察，未列本实验局限）。
brief.reuse: 作者提供了开源仿真框架，可模拟选举领导机制、构建社会图并计算中心性指标、对 leader 话语做情感分析。

bf3b611e10312e5b.text: Background: Traditional research on collaborative learning scaffolding is often time-consuming and resource-heavy, which hinders the rapid iteration and optimization of instructional strategies. LLM-based multi-agent systems have recently emerged as a powerful tool to simulate complex social interactions and provide a novel paradigm for educational research. Objectives: This study proposes an LLM-based multi-agent simulation approach to investigate collaborative learning processes and the effectiveness of instructional scaffolds prior to actual classroom deployment. The research specifically examines the feasibility of simulating group discussions and the alignment of these simulations with established learning science theories. Methods: The simulation system was implemented using the MetaGPT framework and GPT-4o, comprising one teacher agent and five distinct student roles (Leader, Supporter, Expounder, Rebutter, and Summarizer). Two scaffolding strategies, "Deep Think before Speak" and "Direct Speak", were compared across ten classical Chinese poetry appreciation tasks. Evaluation was conducted through discourse analysis of quality and behavior. Results and Conclusions: The introduction of the "Deep Think before Speak" scaffold significantly improved the agents' discourse diversity and interaction depth while notably reducing content repetitiveness. Behavioral analysis showed that the scaffold encouraged more complex interaction patterns, such as reflecting, rebutting, and explaining. These findings align with the ICAP framework, as the scaffold prompted agents to move from simple "Active" participation to "Constructive" and "Interactive" knowledge co-construction. This study demonstrates the feasibility and ecological validity of using LLM-based multi-agent systems to simulate authentic collaborative learning dynamics.

b3021f1cba087037.text: Large language models (LLMs) has been widely used for automated negotiation, but their high computational cost and privacy risks limit deployment in privacy-sensitive, on-device settings such as mobile assistants or rescue robots. Small language models (SLMs) offer a viable alternative, yet struggle with the complex emotional dynamics of high-stakes negotiation. We introduces EmoMAS, a Bayesian multi-agent framework that transforms emotional decision-making from reactive to strategic. EmoMAS leverages a Bayesian orchestrator to coordinate three specialized agents: game-theoretic, reinforcement learning, and psychological coherence models. The system fuses their real-time insights to optimize emotional state transitions while continuously updating agent reliability based on negotiation feedback. This mixture-of-agents architecture enables online strategy learning without pre-training. We further introduce four high-stakes, edge-deployable negotiation benchmarks across debt, healthcare, emergency response, and educational domains. Through extensive agent-to-agent simulations across all benchmarks, both SLMs and LLMs equipped with EmoMAS consistently surpass all baseline models in negotiation performance while balancing ethical behavior. These results show that strategic emotional intelligence is also the key driver of negotiation success. By treating emotional expression as a strategic variable within a Bayesian multi-agent optimization framework, EmoMAS establishes a new paradigm for effective, private, and adaptive negotiation AI suitable for high-stakes edge deployment.

b5d6734182857bca.text: LLM-based user simulation is the primary mechanism for end-to-end agent evaluation, yet simulated users are poor proxies for real humans: unconstrained LLM defaults produce a Formalism Ceiling (style match rates of 6-8% against real users), while hand-crafted behavioral directives trigger Directive Amplification, where models hyper-interpret instructions into unnatural behavioral extremes that vary dramatically across simulator models. We present RealUserSim, the first user simulation framework grounded in real behavioral data. From 14,000+ authentic human-LLM conversations (WildChat), we extract 7,275 executable behavioral profiles and use them to ground LLM simulators. A fidelity benchmark (PT3) on 600 conversations across 71+ domains with anti-leakage controls shows that grounded simulation raises match rate from 24.2% to 45.3% across five behavioral dimensions. Agent evaluation on TauBench with 6 simulator models and extensive analysis shows that grounded simulation acts as a realistic stress test, surfacing three failure mechanisms invisible to cooperative simulators (mean -3.2% to -3.5% task success degradation), while Directive Amplification in existing benchmarks produces unrealistic behavior that compromises the validity of agent evaluation.
b5d6734182857bca.abstract_zh:
基于大模型的用户模拟是端到端智能体评测的主要手段，但模拟用户很难代表真人。作者观察到两个问题：不加约束的 LLM 默认输出存在一个“形式天花板”，与真实用户的风格匹配率只有 6-8%；而手工编写的行为指令会触发“指令放大”，模型把指令过度解读成不自然的行为极端，且不同模拟器模型之间差异很大。

RealUserSim 是第一个用真实行为数据做约束的用户模拟框架。作者从 WildChat 的 14,000 多条真实人机对话中提取出 7,275 个可执行的行为档案，用这些档案来约束 LLM 模拟器。他们还构建了保真度基准 PT3，覆盖 71 个以上领域、600 条对话，并做了防泄漏控制。结果显示，有档案约束的模拟把五个行为维度上的匹配率从 24.2% 提高到 45.3%。

在 TauBench 上用 6 个模拟器模型做智能体评测后发现，有约束的模拟相当于一次真实的压力测试，暴露出合作型模拟器看不到的三种失败机制，任务成功率平均下降 3.2 到 3.5 个百分点。而现有基准中的指令放大会产生不真实的行为，损害智能体评测的有效性。
b5d6734182857bca.why: 它给出了用真实对话数据校准 LLM 用户模拟的可复用做法和保真度基准，并实证了现有合作型模拟器会漏掉智能体的真实失败模式，对做智能体评测和合成用户样本的人都直接相关。

resources.name: WildChat 真实人机对话数据集

brief.question: 解决 LLM 用户仿真与真实用户差距过大的问题：无约束的 LLM 默认产生 Formalism Ceiling（与真实用户风格匹配率仅 6-8%），手工行为指令又触发 Directive Amplification，模型过度解读指令产生跨仿真模型差异极大的极端行为，损害 agent 评测的有效性。
brief.setup: 从 WildChat 的 14,000+ 真实人机对话中提取 7,275 个可执行行为画像，用于约束 LLM 仿真器；保真度基准 PT3 覆盖 71+ 领域的 600 段对话，agent 评测在 TauBench 上用 6 个仿真模型进行。
brief.method: 用真实行为数据（行为画像）grounding LLM 仿真器，替代无约束默认或手工行为指令；PT3 基准带 anti-leakage 控制，跨五个行为维度测匹配率。
brief.findings: Grounded 仿真把匹配率从 24.2% 提高到 45.3%（五个行为维度）；在 TauBench 上，grounded 仿真作为真实压力测试，暴露出协作式仿真器看不到的三种失败机制，任务成功率平均下降 3.2% 到 3.5%；现有基准中的 Directive Amplification 产生不真实行为，损害 agent 评测有效性。
brief.validation: 与 WildChat 真实人机对话对比匹配率（24.2% 升至 45.3%），PT3 设有 anti-leakage 控制，并在 TauBench 上用 6 个仿真模型做广泛分析。
brief.reuse: 7,275 个从 WildChat 提取的可执行行为画像，以及 PT3 保真度基准（600 段对话、71+ 领域、anti-leakage 控制）。

b30472b468b7fa63.text: Social network simulation aims to model collective opinion dynamics in large populations, but existing LLM-based simulators mainly focus on aggregate dynamics while largely ignoring individual internal states. This limits their ability to capture opinion reversals driven by gradual individual shifts and makes them unreliable in long-horizon simulations. We propose MF-MDP, a social simulation framework that tightly couples macro-level collective dynamics with micro-level individual states. MF-MDP explicitly models per-agent latent opinion states with a state transition mechanism, combining individual Markov Decision Processes at the micro level with a mean-field collective framework at the macro level. This allows individual behaviors to change internal states gradually rather than trigger instant reactions, enabling the simulator to distinguish agents that are close to switching from those that are far from switching, capture opinion reversals, and maintain accuracy over long horizons. Across real-world events, MF-MDP supports stable simulation of long-horizon social processes with up to 40,000 interactions, compared with about 300 in the baseline MF-LLM, while reducing long-horizon KL divergence by 75.3% (1.2490 to 0.3089) and reversal KL by 66.9% (1.6425 to 0.5434), significantly mitigating the drift observed in MF-LLM. Code is available at ai4ss.github.io/M2Sim.

b41cc1d199c45efc.text: In the real economy, modern decision-making is fundamentally challenged by high-dimensional, multimodal environments, which are further complicated by agent heterogeneity and combinatorial data sparsity. This paper introduces a Multi-Agent Large Language Model-based Economic Sandbox (MALLES), leveraging the inherent generalization capabilities of large-sacle models to establish a unified simulation framework applicable to cross-domain and cross-category scenarios. Central to our approach is a preference learning paradigm in which LLMs are economically aligned via post-training on extensive, heterogeneous transaction records across diverse product categories. This methodology enables the models to internalize and transfer latent consumer preference patterns, thereby mitigating the data sparsity issues prevalent in individual categories. To enhance simulation stability, we implement a mean-field mechanism designed to model the dynamic interactions between the product environment and customer populations, effectively stabilizing sampling processes within high-dimensional decision spaces. Furthermore, we propose a multi-agent discussion framework wherein specialized agents collaboratively process extensive product information. This architecture distributes cognitive load to alleviate single-agent attention bottlenecks and captures critical decision factors through structured dialogue. Experiments demonstrate that our framework achieves significant improvements in product selection accuracy, purchase quantity prediction, and simulation stability compared to existing economic and financial LLM simulation baselines. Our results substantiate the potential of large language models as a foundational pillar for high-fidelity, scalable decision simulation and latter analysis in the real economy based on foundational database.

b0f1d8f106b350c2.text: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance on standardized social science instruments, but their value for product discovery remains unclear. We investigate whether interview-informed generative agents can simulate user responses in concept testing scenarios. Using in-depth workflow interviews with knowledge workers, we created personalized agents and compared their evaluations of novel AI concepts against the same participants' responses. Our results show that agents are distribution-calibrated but identity-imprecise: they fail to replicate the specific individual they are grounded in, yet approximate population-level response distributions. These findings highlight both the potential and the limits of LLM simulation in design research. While unsuitable as a substitute for individual-level insights, simulation may provide value for early-stage concept screening and iteration, where distributional accuracy suffices. We discuss implications for integrating simulation responsibly into product development workflows.
b0f1d8f106b350c2.abstract_zh:
大语言模型在标准化社会科学量表上表现不错，但它们对产品发现的价值还不清楚。作者研究的问题是：用访谈信息构建的生成式智能体，能否在概念测试场景中模拟真实用户的反应。

做法上，作者先对知识工作者做深度工作流访谈，据此为每位参与者创建个性化智能体，然后让这些智能体评估若干新颖的 AI 概念，并与同一批参与者本人的真实回答做对比。

结果是智能体呈现“分布校准但个体不准”的模式：它们无法复现各自对应的那个具体个体的回答，但能较好地逼近人群层面的回答分布。作者据此判断，这类模拟不适合替代个体层面的用户洞察，但在早期概念筛选和迭代这类只需要分布准确性的场景里可能有价值。论文最后讨论了如何负责任地把仿真整合进产品开发流程。
b0f1d8f106b350c2.why: 它用同一批真人的访谈和回答做了严格对照验证，给出了一个对做用户仿真的人很实用的结论：LLM 智能体适合做人群分布层面的概念筛选，不能当个体替身。

b5f84e7823cdf8cb.text: Deploying large language model (LLM) agents in shared environments introduces a fundamental tension between individual alignment and collective stability: locally rational decisions can impose negative externalities that degrade system-level performance. We propose Socially-Weighted Alignment (SWA), a game-theoretic framework that modifies inference-time decision making by interpolating between an agent's private objective and an estimate of group welfare via a social weight $λ\in[0,1]$. In a shared-resource congestion game with $n$ agents and congestion severity $β$, we show that SWA induces a critical threshold $λ^*=(n-β)/(n-1)$ above which agents no longer have marginal incentive to increase demand under overload, yielding a phase transition from persistent congestion to stable operation near capacity. We further provide an inference-time algorithmic instantiation of SWA that does not require parameter updates or multi-agent reinforcement learning, and use a multi-agent simulation to empirically validate the predicted threshold behavior.

b4efa2faee656a47.text: LLM agents are increasingly used for social simulation, yet emotion is often treated as a transient cue, causing emotional amnesia and weak long-horizon continuity. We present Sentipolis, a framework for emotionally stateful agents that integrates continuous Pleasure-Arousal-Dominance (PAD) representation, dual-speed emotion dynamics, and emotion--memory coupling. Across thousands of interactions over multiple base models and evaluators, Sentipolis improves emotionally grounded behavior, boosting communication, and emotional continuity. Gains are model-dependent: believability increases for higher-capacity models but can drop for smaller ones, and emotion-awareness can mildly reduce adherence to social norms, reflecting a human-like tension between emotion-driven behavior and rule compliance in social simulation. Network-level diagnostics show reciprocal, moderately clustered, and temporally stable relationship structures, supporting the study of cumulative social dynamics such as alliance formation and gradual relationship change.

bcb357fb3381eb40.text: We present a reproducible benchmark for evaluating sim-to-real transfer of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) policies for Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAVs). The platform, based on the Cyber-Physical Mobility Lab (CPM Lab) [1], integrates simulation, a high-fidelity digital twin, and a physical testbed, enabling structured zero-shot evaluation of MARL motion-planning policies. We demonstrate its use by deploying a SigmaRL-trained policy [2] across all three domains, revealing two complementary sources of performance degradation: architectural differences between simulation and hardware control stacks, and the sim-to-real gap induced by increasing environmental realism. The open-source setup enables systematic analysis of sim-to-real challenges in MARL under realistic, reproducible conditions.

b26520b5a9125200.text: The effectiveness of collision-free trajectory planners depends on the quality and diversity of training data, especially for rare scenarios. A widely used approach to improve dataset diversity involves generating realistic synthetic traffic scenarios. However, producing such scenarios remains difficult due to the precision required when scripting them manually or generating them in a single pass. Natural language offers a flexible way to describe scenarios, but existing text-to-simulation pipelines often rely on static snippet retrieval, limited grammar, single-pass decoding, or lack robust executability checks. Moreover, they depend heavily on constrained LLM prompting with minimal post-processing. To address these limitations, we introduce ARISE - Adaptive Refinement and Iterative Scenario Engineering, a multi-stage tool that converts natural language prompts into executable Scenic scripts through iterative LLM-guided refinement. After each generation, ARISE tests script executability in simulation software, feeding structured diagnostics back to the LLM until both syntactic and functional requirements are met. This process significantly reduces the need for manual intervention. Through extensive evaluation, ARISE outperforms the baseline in generating semantically accurate and executable traffic scenarios with greater reliability and robustness.

bf7b99438672f6b8.text: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities in multi-step decision-making, and are increasingly integrated into real-world agentic applications. While existing safety evaluations focus on static interactions or refusal rates, it remains largely underexplored what level of threat these models pose once an adversary successfully assigns them a malicious role. To evaluate this agentic misuse risk, we propose VirtualCrime, a dynamic multi-agent sandbox framework that elicits and measures multi-step criminal behavior from LLMs. We design 40 diverse crime tasks within this framework, covering 11 realistic maps and 14 objectives such as theft, robbery, and kidnapping. We evaluate 8 strong LLMs and find that: (1) even with robust safety alignment, all evaluated models exhibit alarming agentic capabilities to generate and execute detailed multi-step criminal plans when placed in an adversarial red-teaming setting; (2) models frequently suffer from behavioral alignment failures, exhibiting a high propensity for over-harm by escalating to violent means far beyond what the task requires; (3) their most sophisticated criminal behaviors concentrate in social deception and team coordination rather than technical exploitation. Our work highlights a critical gap in current safety paradigms, emphasizing the urgent need for behavioral alignment in autonomous agent deployments.
bf7b99438672f6b8.abstract_zh: 现有 LLM 安全评测多停留在静态交互或拒绝率上，很少考察当攻击者成功给模型分配恶意角色后，模型作为智能体会构成多大威胁。为填补这个空白，作者提出 VirtualCrime，一个动态多智能体沙盒框架，用来诱导并测量 LLM 的多步犯罪行为。框架内设计了 40 个多样的犯罪任务，覆盖 11 张现实风格地图和 14 种目标，包括盗窃、抢劫和绑架。作者评测了 8 个强 LLM，得到三点发现。第一，即使经过稳健的安全对齐，所有被测模型在对抗性红队设定下都表现出令人警惕的智能体能力，能生成并执行详细的多步犯罪计划。第二，模型频繁出现行为对齐失败，倾向过度伤害，把手段升级到远超任务所需的暴力程度。第三，模型最复杂的犯罪行为集中在社会欺骗和团队协调上，而不是技术性利用。作者据此指出当前安全范式存在关键缺口，强调自主智能体部署中行为对齐的紧迫性。
bf7b99438672f6b8.why: 它把安全评测从拒绝率推进到沙盒里的多步行为层面，给出的“过度伤害”和“社会欺骗强于技术利用”两个发现对做智能体红队推演和行为对齐的人都有直接参考价值。

b6b75bba692719e4.text: High-fidelity agent initialization is crucial for credible Agent-Based Modeling across diverse domains. A robust framework should be Topic-Adaptive, capturing macro-level joint distributions while ensuring micro-level individual rationality. Existing approaches fall into two categories: static data-based retrieval methods that fail to adapt to unseen topics absent from the data, and LLM-based generation methods that lack macro-level distribution awareness, resulting in inconsistencies between micro-level persona attributes and reality. To address these problems, we propose HAG, a Hierarchical Agent Generation framework that formalizes population generation as a two-stage decision process. Firstly, utilizing a World Knowledge Model to infer hierarchical conditional probabilities to construct the Topic-Adaptive Tree, achieving macro-level distribution alignment. Then, grounded real-world data, instantiation and agentic augmentation are carried out to ensure micro-level consistency. Given the lack of specialized evaluation, we establish a multi-domain benchmark and a comprehensive PACE evaluation framework. Extensive experiments show that HAG significantly outperforms representative baselines, reducing population alignment errors by an average of 37.7% and enhancing sociological consistency by 18.8%.

b73647dc4bc61749.text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate human users in interactive settings such as therapy, education, and social role-play. While these simulations enable scalable training and evaluation of AI agents, off-the-shelf LLMs often drift from their assigned personas, contradict earlier statements, or abandon role-appropriate behavior. We introduce a unified framework for evaluating and improving persona consistency in LLM-generated dialogue. We define three automatic metrics: prompt-to-line consistency, line-to-line consistency, and Q&A consistency, that capture different types of persona drift and validate each against human annotations. Using these metrics as reward signals, we apply multi-turn reinforcement learning to fine-tune LLMs for three user roles: a patient, a student, and a social chat partner. Our method reduces inconsistency by over 55%, resulting in more coherent and faithful simulated users.
b73647dc4bc61749.abstract_zh:
大模型越来越多地被用来在治疗、教育、社交角色扮演等交互场景里模拟人类用户，这类模拟可以规模化地训练和评测 AI 智能体。但直接拿来用的现成大模型经常偏离被分配的人设，与之前说过的话矛盾，或者放弃符合角色的行为。
作者提出了一个统一的框架，用来评测和改进大模型生成对话中的人设一致性。他们定义了三种自动指标：prompt 到台词的一致性、台词之间的一致性、问答一致性，分别捕捉不同类型的人设漂移，并用人工标注验证了每种指标的有效性。以这些指标作为奖励信号，作者用多轮强化学习微调大模型，覆盖三类用户角色：病人、学生和社交聊天伙伴。结果显示，不一致行为减少了超过 55%，模拟出的用户更连贯、更忠实于角色。材料没有报告与真实用户数据的进一步对比，方法主要在指标层面验证。
b73647dc4bc61749.why: 它把“人设漂移”拆成三种可自动度量、且经人工标注验证的指标，并直接用这些指标当奖励做多轮强化学习，给做人类行为仿真的研究者提供了一套可复用的评测和训练配方。

b827931c22162f86.text: Recent deep trajectory predictors (e.g., Jiang et al., 2023; Zhou et al., 2022) have achieved strong average accuracy but remain unreliable in complex long-tail driving scenarios. These limitations reveal the weakness of the prevailing "one-model-fits-all" paradigm, particularly in safety-critical urban contexts where simpler physics-based models can occasionally outperform advanced networks (Kalman, 1960). To bridge this gap, we propose a dynamic multi-expert gating framework that adaptively selects the most reliable trajectory predictor among a physics-informed LSTM, a Transformer, and a fine-tuned GameFormer on a per-sample basis. Our method leverages internal model signals (meta-features) such as stability and uncertainty (Gal and Ghahramani, 2016), which we demonstrate to be substantially more informative than geometric scene descriptors. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to formulate trajectory expert selection as a pairwise-ranking problem over internal model signals (Burges et al., 2005), directly optimizing decision quality without requiring post-hoc calibration. Evaluated on the nuPlan-mini dataset (Caesar et al., 2021) with 1,287 samples, our LLM-enhanced tri-expert gate achieves a Final Displacement Error (FDE) of 2.567 m, representing a 9.5 percent reduction over GameFormer (2.835 m), and realizes 57.8 percent of the oracle performance bound. In open-loop simulations, after trajectory horizon alignment, the same configuration reduces FDE on left-turn scenarios by approximately 10 percent, demonstrating consistent improvements across both offline validation and open-loop evaluation. These results indicate that adaptive hybrid systems enhance trajectory reliability in safety-critical autonomous driving, providing a practical pathway beyond static single-model paradigms.

b27f075fff46c7e5.text: Multi-agent social interaction has clearly benefited from Large Language Models. However, current simulation systems still face challenges such as difficulties in scaling to diverse scenarios and poor reusability due to a lack of modular design. To address these issues, we designed and developed a modular, object-oriented framework that organically integrates various base classes through a hierarchical structure, harvesting scalability and reusability. We inherited the framework to realize common derived classes. Additionally, a memory summarization mechanism is proposed to filter and distill relevant information from raw memory data, prioritizing contextually salient events and interactions. By selecting and combining some necessary derived classes, we customized a specific simulated environment. Utilizing this simulated environment, we successfully simulated human interactions on social media, replicating real-world online social behaviors. The source code for the project will be released and evolve.

bde8d07ca49bc0d5.text: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled new possibilities in simulating complex physiological systems. We introduce Organ-Agents, a multi-agent framework that simulates human physiology via LLM-driven agents. Each Simulator models a specific system (e.g., cardiovascular, renal, immune). Training consists of supervised fine-tuning on system-specific time-series data, followed by reinforcement-guided coordination using dynamic reference selection and error correction. We curated data from 7,134 sepsis patients and 7,895 controls, generating high-resolution trajectories across 9 systems and 125 variables. Organ-Agents achieved high simulation accuracy on 4,509 held-out patients, with per-system MSEs <0.16 and robustness across SOFA-based severity strata. External validation on 22,689 ICU patients from two hospitals showed moderate degradation under distribution shifts with stable simulation. Organ-Agents faithfully reproduces critical multi-system events (e.g., hypotension, hyperlactatemia, hypoxemia) with coherent timing and phase progression. Evaluation by 15 critical care physicians confirmed realism and physiological plausibility (mean Likert ratings 3.9 and 3.7). Organ-Agents also enables counterfactual simulations under alternative sepsis treatment strategies, generating trajectories and APACHE II scores aligned with matched real-world patients. In downstream early warning tasks, classifiers trained on synthetic data showed minimal AUROC drops (<0.04), indicating preserved decision-relevant patterns. These results position Organ-Agents as a credible, interpretable, and generalizable digital twin for precision diagnosis, treatment simulation, and hypothesis testing in critical care.
bde8d07ca49bc0d5.abstract_zh:
作者提出 Organ-Agents，一个用大模型驱动的多智能体框架来模拟人体生理。每个 Simulator 智能体负责一个系统，比如心血管、肾脏、免疫。训练分两步：先在系统专属的时序数据上做监督微调，再用动态参考选择和误差修正做强化引导的协调。数据来自 7134 名脓毒症患者和 7895 名对照，生成了覆盖 9 个系统、125 个变量的高分辨率轨迹。

在 4509 名留出患者上，各系统 MSE 均低于 0.16，且在按 SOFA 分层的不同严重度组上都保持稳健。在两所医院 22689 名 ICU 患者上做外部验证，分布偏移下性能中度下降但仿真保持稳定。模型能忠实再现低血压、高乳酸血症、低氧血症等多系统关键事件，时序和阶段演进连贯。15 位重症医生评估认为其真实感和生理合理性可信，平均 Likert 评分分别为 3.9 和 3.7。

框架还支持反事实仿真：在替代脓毒症治疗策略下生成轨迹和 APACHE II 评分，与匹配的真实患者对齐。在下游早期预警任务中，用合成数据训练的分类器 AUROC 下降不超过 0.04，说明决策相关的模式被保留。作者认为 Organ-Agents 可作为重症监护中精准诊断、治疗仿真和假设检验的数字孪生。局限方面，材料提到分布偏移下性能有中度下降。
bde8d07ca49bc0d5.why: 它把多智能体仿真从社会和军事场景推进到人体生理系统，用真实 ICU 数据训练和验证，并展示了反事实治疗仿真这条仿真推演独有的能力，对做医疗仿真和数字孪生的研究者是可复用的方法。

brief.question: 用 LLM 智能体仿真人体生理系统，特别是重症监护中脓毒症患者的多系统生理动态，用于精准诊断、治疗模拟和假设检验。
brief.setup: Organ-Agents 是多智能体框架，每个 Simulator 智能体对应一个生理系统（如心血管、肾脏、免疫），共覆盖 9 个系统、125 个变量。训练数据来自 7,134 名脓毒症患者和 7,895 名对照，生成高分辨率生理轨迹。
brief.method: 先在各系统的时序数据上做监督微调，再用强化学习引导多智能体协调，机制包括动态参考选择和误差修正。
brief.findings: 在 4,509 名留出患者上各系统 MSE <0.16，按 SOFA 严重度分层表现稳健。能忠实再现低血压、高乳酸血症、低氧血症等多系统事件，时序和阶段演进连贯。反事实仿真可生成替代脓毒症治疗策略下的轨迹和 APACHE II 分数，与匹配的真实患者一致。用合成数据训练的早期预警分类器 AUROC 下降 <0.04。

b019af99666c5b59.text: Recent advances in large language models have demonstrated strong reasoning and role-playing capabilities, opening new opportunities for agent-based social simulations. However, most existing agents' implementations are scenario-tailored, without a unified framework to guide the design. This lack of a general social agent limits their ability to generalize across different social contexts and to produce consistent, realistic behaviors. To address this challenge, we propose a theory-informed framework that provides a systematic design process for LLM-based social agents. Our framework is grounded in principles from Social Cognition Theory and introduces three key modules: motivation, action planning, and learning. These modules jointly enable agents to reason about their goals, plan coherent actions, and adapt their behavior over time, leading to more flexible and contextually appropriate responses. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our theory-driven agents reproduce realistic human behavior patterns under complex conditions, achieving up to 75% lower deviation from real-world behavioral data across multiple fidelity metrics compared to classical generative baselines. Ablation studies further show that removing motivation, planning, or learning modules increases errors by 1.5 to 3.2 times, confirming their distinct and essential contributions to generating realistic and coherent social behaviors.
b019af99666c5b59.abstract_zh: 现有的大语言模型智能体社会仿真大多是针对具体场景定制的实现，缺少统一的设计框架，导致智能体难以泛化到不同社会情境，行为也不够一致和真实。作者为此提出一个理论驱动的框架，用社会认知理论的原则指导 LLM 社会智能体的系统化设计，包含三个模块：动机、行动规划和学习。动机模块让智能体推理自己的目标，规划模块生成连贯的行动，学习模块让行为随时间适应调整，三者共同产生更灵活、更贴合情境的响应。实验部分，作者在复杂条件下测试这些智能体，发现它们能复现真实的人类行为模式，在多个保真度指标上与真实行为数据的偏差比经典生成式基线最多低 75%。消融实验进一步验证了各模块的贡献：去掉动机、规划或学习中的任何一个，误差都会增加 1.5 到 3.2 倍，说明三个模块各自独立且必要。局限方面，摘要未展开讨论框架在哪些具体场景验证、计算成本如何。
b019af99666c5b59.why: 它把散乱的场景定制式社会智能体实现收进一个有理论依据的模块化框架，并给出各模块必要性的消融证据，做社会仿真的人可以直接对照这套动机-规划-学习结构来设计自己的智能体。

brief.question: 现有 LLM 社会智能体多为场景定制实现，缺少统一设计框架，难以跨社会情境泛化并产生一致、真实的行为。作者要设计一个通用的 LLM 社会智能体框架。
brief.setup: 未说明具体智能体数量、环境和时间尺度。框架基于 Social Cognition Theory，用于 LLM-based social agents。
brief.method: 提出 theory-informed 框架，含三个模块：motivation（推理目标）、action planning（规划连贯行动）、learning（随时间调整行为）。
brief.findings: 理论驱动的智能体在复杂条件下复现了真实人类行为模式，与真实世界行为数据的偏差比经典生成式基线低最多 75%（跨多个 fidelity 指标）。消融实验中去掉任一模块，误差增加 1.5 到 3.2 倍。
brief.validation: 与真实世界行为数据对比，偏差最多降低 75%；另有消融实验验证三个模块各自的必要性。

bb672c42425bf3a3.text: Recent advances in large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized mobile robots, including unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), enabling their intelligent operation within Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems. However, LLMs still face challenges from logical reasoning and complex decision-making, leading to concerns about the reliability of LLM-driven UAV operations in IoT applications. In this paper, we propose a closed-loop LLM-driven UAV operation code generation framework that enables reliable UAV operations powered by effective feedback and refinement using two LLM modules, i.e., a Code Generator and an Evaluator. Our framework transforms numerical state observations from UAV operations into semantic trajectory descriptions to enhance the evaluator LLM's understanding of UAV dynamics for precise feedback generation. Our framework also enables a simulation-based refinement process, and hence eliminates the risks to physical UAVs caused by incorrect code execution during the refinement. Extensive experiments on UAV control tasks with different complexities are conducted. The experimental results show that our framework can achieve reliable UAV operations using LLMs, which significantly outperforms baseline methods in terms of success rate and completeness with the increase of task complexity.

b389fda76506769e.text: Peer-to-peer (P2P) trading is increasingly recognized as a key mechanism for decentralized market regulation, yet existing approaches often lack robust frameworks to ensure fairness. This paper presents FairMarket-RL, a novel hybrid framework that combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) to enable fairness-aware trading agents. In a simulated P2P microgrid with multiple sellers and buyers, the LLM acts as a real-time fairness critic, evaluating each trading episode using two metrics: Fairness-To-Buyer (FTB) and Fairness-Between-Sellers (FBS). These fairness scores are integrated into agent rewards through scheduled λ-coefficients, forming an adaptive LLM-guided reward shaping loop that replaces brittle, rule-based fairness constraints. Agents are trained using Independent Proximal Policy Optimization (IPPO) and achieve equitable outcomes, fulfilling over 90% of buyer demand, maintaining fair seller margins, and consistently reaching FTB and FBS scores above 0.80. The training process demonstrates that fairness feedback improves convergence, reduces buyer shortfalls, and narrows profit disparities between sellers. With its language-based critic, the framework scales naturally, and its extension to a large power distribution system with household prosumers illustrates its practical applicability. FairMarket-RL thus offers a scalable, equity-driven solution for autonomous trading in decentralized energy systems.

bdd0167d50d92395.text: Conversational Recommender Systems (CRSs) engage users in multi-turn interactions to deliver personalized recommendations. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) further enhances these systems by enabling more natural and dynamic user interactions. However, a key challenge remains in understanding how personality traits shape conversational recommendation outcomes. Psychological evidence highlights the influence of personality traits on user interaction behaviors. To address this, we introduce an LLM-based personality-aware user simulation for CRSs (PerCRS). The user agent induces customizable personality traits and preferences, while the system agent possesses the persuasion capability to simulate realistic interaction in CRSs. We incorporate multi-aspect evaluation to ensure robustness and conduct extensive analysis from both user and system perspectives. Experimental results demonstrate that state-of-the-art LLMs can effectively generate diverse user responses aligned with specified personality traits, thereby prompting CRSs to dynamically adjust their recommendation strategies. Our experimental analysis offers empirical insights into the impact of personality traits on the outcomes of conversational recommender systems.

b1f9e7823c80878f.text: Companies across all economic sectors continue to deploy large language models at a rapid pace. Reinforcement learning is experiencing a resurgence of interest due to its association with the fine-tuning of language models from human feedback. Tool-chain language models control task-specific agents; if the converse has not already appeared, it soon will. In this paper, we present what we believe is the first investigation of an intelligent trading agent based on continuous deep reinforcement learning that also controls a large language model with which it can post to a social media feed observed by other traders. We empirically investigate the performance and impact of such an agent in a simulated financial market, finding that it learns to optimize its total reward, and thereby augment its profit, by manipulating the sentiment of the posts it produces. The paper concludes with discussion, limitations, and suggestions for future work.

b64c46d2b8b7287e.text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being used to simulate human-like decision making in agent-based financial market models (ABMs). As models become more powerful and accessible, researchers can now incorporate individual LLM decisions into ABM environments. However, integration may introduce inherent biases that need careful evaluation. In this paper we test three state-of-the-art GPT models for bias using two model sampling approaches: one-shot and few-shot API queries. We observe significant variations in distributions of outputs between specific models, and model sub versions, with GPT-4o-Mini-2024-07-18 showing notably better performance (32-43% yes responses) compared to GPT-4-0125-preview's extreme bias (98-99% yes responses). We show that sampling methods and model sub-versions significantly impact results: repeated independent API calls produce different distributions compared to batch sampling within a single call. While no current GPT model can simultaneously achieve a uniform distribution and Markovian properties in one-shot testing, few-shot sampling can approach uniform distributions under certain conditions. We explore the Temperature parameter, providing a definition and comparative results. We further compare our results to true random binary series and test specifically for the common human bias of Negative Recency - finding LLMs have a mixed ability to 'beat' humans in this one regard. These findings emphasise the critical importance of careful LLM integration into ABMs for financial markets and more broadly.

b93cc93958682de3.text: Social media platforms like X(Twitter) and Reddit are vital to global communication. However, advancements in Large Language Model (LLM) technology give rise to social media bots with unprecedented intelligence. These bots adeptly simulate human profiles, conversations, and interactions, disseminating large amounts of false information and posing significant challenges to platform regulation. To better understand and counter these threats, we innovatively design BotSim, a malicious social botnet simulation powered by LLM. BotSim mimics the information dissemination patterns of real-world social networks, creating a virtual environment composed of intelligent agent bots and real human users. In the temporal simulation constructed by BotSim, these advanced agent bots autonomously engage in social interactions such as posting and commenting, effectively modeling scenarios of information flow and user interaction. Building on the BotSim framework, we construct a highly human-like, LLM-driven bot dataset called BotSim-24 and benchmark multiple bot detection strategies against it. The experimental results indicate that detection methods effective on traditional bot datasets perform worse on BotSim-24, highlighting the urgent need for new detection strategies to address the cybersecurity threats posed by these advanced bots.

b60572db55616b6c.text: Surveys are widely used in social sciences to understand human behavior, but their implementation often involves iterative adjustments that demand significant effort and resources. To this end, researchers have increasingly turned to large language models (LLMs) to simulate human behavior. While existing studies have focused on distributional similarities, individual-level comparisons remain underexplored. Building upon prior work, we investigate whether providing LLMs with respondents' prior information can replicate both statistical distributions and individual decision-making patterns using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), a well-established causal analysis method. We also introduce the concept of the LLM-Mirror, user personas generated by supplying respondent-specific information to the LLM. By comparing responses generated by the LLM-Mirror with actual individual survey responses, we assess its effectiveness in replicating individual-level outcomes. Our findings show that: (1) PLS-SEM analysis shows LLM-generated responses align with human responses, (2) LLMs, when provided with respondent-specific information, are capable of reproducing individual human responses, and (3) LLM-Mirror responses closely follow human responses at the individual level. These findings highlight the potential of LLMs as a complementary tool for pre-testing surveys and optimizing research design.

b79b3d5976ec5a92.text: Social norms play a crucial role in guiding agents towards understanding and adhering to standards of behavior, thus reducing social conflicts within multi-agent systems (MASs). However, current LLM-based (or generative) MASs lack the capability to be normative. In this paper, we propose a novel architecture, named CRSEC, to empower the emergence of social norms within generative MASs. Our architecture consists of four modules: Creation & Representation, Spreading, Evaluation, and Compliance. This addresses several important aspects of the emergent processes all in one: (i) where social norms come from, (ii) how they are formally represented, (iii) how they spread through agents' communications and observations, (iv) how they are examined with a sanity check and synthesized in the long term, and (v) how they are incorporated into agents' planning and actions. Our experiments deployed in the Smallville sandbox game environment demonstrate the capability of our architecture to establish social norms and reduce social conflicts within generative MASs. The positive outcomes of our human evaluation, conducted with 30 evaluators, further affirm the effectiveness of our approach. Our project can be accessed via the following link: https://github.com/sxswz213/CRSEC.

b527f71069261b75.text: This paper explores the open research problem of understanding the social behaviors of LLM-based agents. Using Avalon as a testbed, we employ system prompts to guide LLM agents in gameplay. While previous studies have touched on gameplay with LLM agents, research on their social behaviors is lacking. We propose a novel framework, tailored for Avalon, features a multi-agent system facilitating efficient communication and interaction. We evaluate its performance based on game success and analyze LLM agents' social behaviors. Results affirm the framework's effectiveness in creating adaptive agents and suggest LLM-based agents' potential in navigating dynamic social interactions. By examining collaboration and confrontation behaviors, we offer insights into this field's research and applications. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/3DAgentWorld/LLM-Game-Agent.
